provenance.source: CDR micro-benchmark of the stack's ROS 2 message types (mw_bench.cpp) + published executor latency
provenance.notes: FALLBACK (spec V4 failed: no Docker/ROS 2). Serialization/deserialization/copy measured on this Mac (Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.4.1.1), -O2), scaled by mac_to_target_scale=3.0 (ASSUMPTION, see scaling.rationale). Executor dispatch from the cited study: average hot-path latency divided by its 5 hops, not scaled (platform of the study, assumption). events_dispatch_ns uses the StaticSingleThreadedExecutor figure as a proxy (assumption: both avoid rebuilding the wait set). The per-hop figures include DDS delivery and thread wake-ups, not only executor bookkeeping.
references: Klepsydra, 'The ring-buffer ROS2 executor: a novel approach for real-time ROS2 Space applications', 2023, Table I (Autoware reference system, N=64, average critical-path latency); hot-path definition from github.com/ros-realtime/reference-system autoware_reference_system README

copy.notes: copy transport: serialize into a CDR buffer, DDS copies it into its history / shared segment, the reader copies it out, then deserializes: 2 full-buffer copies besides ser/deser.

zero_copy.notes: loaned messages (bounded/plain types or type adaptation): refcount + pointer hand-off measured, plus 500 ns assumed for the loan/return calls into the RMW. Requires fixed-size message types.

published.source: Klepsydra, 'The ring-buffer ROS2 executor: a novel approach for real-time ROS2 Space applications', 2023, Table I (Autoware reference system, N=64, average critical-path latency); hot-path definition from github.com/ros-realtime/reference-system autoware_reference_system README

scaling.rationale: Assumption. Mac P-core about 3.5-4 GHz, very wide OoO; VX-1 app core 2.0 GHz, IPC 2.0 assumed (vx1.yaml). Measured single-core bulk copy here is about 55 GB/s; a VX-1 core is assumed to sustain about 25 GB/s. Both ratios are near 3.
